_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: render indices 2, 4, 6 ONLY (= printed Pages 3, 5, 7 of 8). All 8 indices accounted for by reading contact.png first and then confirming each page full-size: idx0 = bilingual cover (Hindi bullets above English bullets, no questions, 'Page 1 of 8', code 310 C); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Section A (khand-ka) Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION-A Q1-6; idx3 = HINDI Section B (khand-kha) Q7-10 + Section C (khand-ga) header + Q11-12; idx4 = ENGLISH SECTION-B Q7-10 + SECTION-C header + Q11-12; idx5 = HINDI Q13 + case study Q14; idx6 = ENGLISH Q13 + Case Study Q14; idx7 = BLANK (printed 'Page 8 of 8', carries only QR codes, the 310 C code, a lone asterisk and the footer). The alternating hypothesis HELD EXACTLY and all three documented failure modes were checked for and did NOT occur: I read the top of every odd page and the last page and NONE carried English overflow (each language block is a self-contained mirrored page, so no question straddles a language boundary); there is no English-only final page (idx7 is blank); and there is no mid-paper parity inversion (Hindi and English occupy exactly 3 pages each, Hindi first). Question numbers run 1 to 14 unbroken with every sub-part present. STRUCTURE CONFIRMED off idx2 and the cover: 14 questions, 40 marks, 2 hours; Section A Q1-6 @2 = 12, Section B Q7-10 @3 = 12, Section C Q11-13 @4 = 12 plus Q14 case study 2+2 = 4; total 40. NO MCQs ANYWHERE - every row is subjective, so no options and no answer letters. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so the FOUR OR-alternatives were established by walking the marking scheme question by question (it reprints both branches under a centred OR): the scheme prints an OR block for exactly Q6, Q8, Q9 and Q12 and for NO other question - Q1-Q5, Q7, Q10, Q11, Q13 and Q14 each run straight from stem to Sol. with no OR. The 40-mark sum was NOT used as the check, since it is structurally blind to a missed alternative. All 11 marking-scheme pages accounted for: ms p00-p01 are the examiner's general instructions (items 1-17, no question content), ms p02-p10 are the scheme proper, running Q1 to Q14 and closing with '* * *'. OVERLAP WITH 65/3/1: judged by CONTENT against data/2022-65-3-1.questions.json, not by number - 15 of the 19 rows are the SAME questions, reshuffled (this paper's Q1=65/3/1 Q4, Q2=Q3, Q4=Q5, Q5=Q1, Q6a/b=Q6a/b, Q8a/b=Q9a/b, Q9a/b=Q8a/b, Q11=Q13, Q12a/b=Q12a/b, Q14a/b=Q14a/b) and their stems are reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE from that file after confirming each against my own page image, so they dedup at commit. Genuinely NEW here: Q3 (dy/dx = (3e^2x+3e^4x)/(e^x+e^-x); 65/3/1's Q2 is the unrelated e^(dy/dx) = x^2), Q7 (shortest distance between two lines; 65/3/1's Q10 is a coplanarity proof), Q10 (integral of sin|x|+cos|x| over -pi/2..pi/2; 65/3/1's Q7 is the 1/(1+e^sin x) definite integral) and Q13 (area enclosed by y^2 = x, x = 1/4, y = 0, x = 1; 65/3/1's Q11 is 4x^2 = y with y = 8x+12). plan.txt got the COUNT right (4 new) and the IDENTITIES largely wrong: it lists TRANSCRIBE Q2, Q5, Q11, Q13 of which only Q13 is genuinely new, and its SKIP list wrongly skips Q3 and Q10, which are both new. It was therefore used only as a hint, exactly as the brief warns. THE PLANE: Q1 (distance of a point from a plane) and Q11 (line meets plane) are filed on 'The Plane', the subtopic added to the live Three Dimensional Geometry axis on 2026-08-19 for exactly this 2022 Term-2 need; no flag raised. MARKING-SCHEME DEFECT: on ms p04 the marks cell for 6.(b) prints '3' where Section A carries 2 marks each - the question paper prints 2 for Q6, and the scheme's own sub-total row for that answer reads 2, so the 3 is a marking-scheme typo. Our rows carry 2; see the flag on Q6b. No solutions written: this pipeline authors them later from the marking scheme. TYPOGRAPHY NOTE: the paper is inconsistent about italicising variables - it sets x and lambda italic but y and z upright roman in Q1, Q9 and Q13, and prints the differential operator as upright 'd'. That is typesetting, not mathematics, and is normalised to ordinary LaTeX italics throughout. FIGURES: the only printed artwork in the whole paper is the decorative flower photograph in Q14 (idx 6), which carries no data; Q13's graph is drawn BY the candidate (the scheme awards a mark for 'Correct Figure'), so nothing in this paper is figure-dependent.

questions.stem: If the distance of the point (1, 1, 1) from the plane \(x - y + z + \lambda = 0\) is \(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\), find the value(s) of \(\lambda\).

Write the projection of the vector \((\vec{b} + \vec{c})\) on the vector \(\vec{a}\), where \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\).
Find the general solution of the differential equation : \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3e^{2x} + 3e^{4x}}{e^x + e^{-x}}\)
Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability distribution of the number of spade cards.

questions.stem: The probability that A hits the target is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and the probability that B hits it, is \(\dfrac{2}{5}\). If both try to hit the target independently, find the probability that the target is hit.

Find the shortest distance between the following lines : \(\vec{r} = 3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k} + \lambda(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})\) and \(\vec{r} = (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \mu(7\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + \hat{k})\).

The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by vectors \(2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). Find the unit vector parallel to one of its diagonals. Also, find the area of the parallelogram.

If \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j}\) are such that the vector \((\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b})\) is perpendicular to vector \(\vec{c}\), then find the value of \(\lambda\).
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^2 \cdot e^x\), given \(y(1) = 0\).
Find the general solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\log y - \log x + 1)\).

Find the distance of the point (1, -2, 9) from the point of intersection of the line \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k} + \lambda(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\) and the plane \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 10\).
Find the area of the region enclosed by the curves \(y^2 = x\), \(x = \dfrac{1}{4}\), \(y = 0\) and \(x = 1\), using integration.
